title: R3 disaster-recovery completion composition
description: Objective: make `recovery.complete` a real durable command that can clear QUIESCED only for the exact installed restore and fully reconciled external world. Deliverable: a daemon recovery-completion service that recomputes a versioned R3 recovery digest over BackupGeneration/cursor, RecoveryAnchor install, incarnation/key epoch, configured inventory coverage and dispositions, verifies a current HUMAN R3 approval with reason and recent step-up bound to that digest, then calls the existing project reducer and durable store exactly once. MEASURED GAP at HEAD 1ce0059: core `RecoveryCompletionWitness` and `reduceProject` exist and generic policy supports R3, but no daemon service builds the witness, no canonical recovery digest exists, and no approval is bound to restore/inventory bytes. NOT in scope: minting the restore identity, installing slots, enumerating external state, weakening the embargo, UI controls, GO_QUIESCE/GO_ACTIVATE, or tests/fault. Hard dependencies: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a, task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683, task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587, and task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa must be DONE and consumed. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion.* plus minimal command-registry/index wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test.
definitionOfDone: The production service recomputes one canonical versioned digest over project, backup generation/cursor/RPO, installed anchor slot and command, current incarnation/key epoch, exact configured inventory class set, coverage proofs, item dispositions, quarantine refs, and reconciliation digest; callers cannot supply the accepted digest as authority.

Only a current HUMAN approval classified R3 and carrying a non-empty reason plus recent step-up reference, itself bound to that exact digest/incarnation/project, can authorize completion; system-policy, stale, carried-forward, mismatched, or weaker approvals refuse.

Missing/unverifiable evidence or unresolved UNKNOWN/quarantined inventory returns `UNKNOWN_TRUTH` or `RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` from its originating layer; digest mismatch returns `RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH` at layer `RECOVERY_COMPLETION`; tests pin which layer refused first.

A valid request durably commits exactly one `recovery.complete` decision/event using the existing reducer, changes the selected database from QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED to READY, and releases the effect embargo only in the same committed authority sequence; replay returns the stored decision without a second transition.
Any post-approval change to anchor, generation, key epoch, coverage, inventory, disposition, quarantine, policy, reason, or step-up binding invalidates completion and leaves the project quiesced.
Focused tests use the shipped store, core reducer, policy approval, anchor, and inventory surfaces—not reimplemented helpers—and mutation-check the production digest comparison.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN part 1 — evidence gathering and digest comparison, in apps/daemon/src/recovery/recovery-completion.ts (+ its one-line .js bridge). Decode the envelope first: exact payload keys, nothing else (structural refusal precedes every evidence read). The request carries POINTERS ONLY — reconciliationDigest, the approval record, the approval command, and expectedVersion — and NEVER the accepted digest itself; DoD 1 forbids a caller supplying the digest as authority, so the service recomputes it from what it reads. Read, in this order, wrapping each in try/catch and mapping a thrown DurableStoreError to RECOVERY_COMPLETION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE with its code in upstream: `readRecoveryReconciliation(store, reconciliationDigest)`; then the record's truth/coordinator/upstream gate; then the QUARANTINED-item gate; then `readInstalledRestore(store, record.projectId)`; then `readAnchoredIncarnation`; then `stateOf(readDurableLedger(store, record.projectId), record.projectId)`. Cross-check that the record's incarnationRef, keyEpochRef and anchorBindingDigest agree with the anchor and the installed restore, and that the project is QUIESCED with recoveryRequired true — any disagreement is RECOVERY_COMPLETION_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH, any absence RECOVERY_COMPLETION_EVIDENCE_ABSENT, both at RECOVERY_COMPLETION with the upstream layer preserved. Snapshot every store-returned object/array through own enumerable data descriptors before use. Then call `recoveryCompletionDigest` over the assembled server-read tuple and compare it to the approval record's `exactRevisionHash`; inequality is RECOVERY_COMPLETION_DIGEST_MISMATCH at RECOVERY_COMPLETION. Keep this file <=250 physical lines measured with `grep -c ''` — PowerShell Measure-Object -Line undercounts — and split before 400.

Decode: exact 9-key envelope, kind and schemaVersion pinned, ISO decidedAt, safe non-negative integer expectedVersion, then the exact 3-key payload allow-list with reconciliationDigest required hex64. Section values pass through untouched; an extra payload key is REFUSED, never dropped, so a smuggled `witness` or `truthClass` cannot look honoured. Structural refusal precedes every store read.

Evidence order, each store call in its own try/catch mapping a thrown DurableStoreError to RECOVERY_COMPLETION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE with the store code in upstream: readRecoveryReconciliation (its UNKNOWN_TRUTH / RECOVERY_INVENTORY answer and the ledger's own upstream tuple surfaced verbatim) -> record truth/coordinator gate -> QUARANTINED-item gate -> readInstalledRestore -> readAnchoredIncarnation -> stateOf(readDurableLedger(...)). Eight cross-checks then run as one conjunction: anchor keyEpochRef / bindingDigest / backupGenerationDigest against the record, installed restore incarnationRef / keyEpochRef / generationDigest against the record, restore restoreCommandId against the anchor's, and record.projectId against the commanded project; then lifecycle QUIESCED with recoveryRequired true. Absence is RECOVERY_COMPLETION_EVIDENCE_ABSENT (carrying the restore controller's own code+layer in upstream), disagreement is RECOVERY_COMPLETION_EVIDENCE_MISMATCH.

Project state is snapshotted through own ENUMERABLE data descriptors with accessors filtered out and the result frozen, so no field can answer differently on a second read. The record, the restore and the anchor arrive already decoded from durable bytes, not from caller objects.

THE CALLER NEVER SUPPLIES THE DIGEST. The payload has no field that could carry it: the service assembles the tuple from what it read and calls recoveryCompletionDigest itself, then compares against the approval's exactRevisionHash. readRecoveryCompletionEvidence is exported so an operator learns the digest to approve through the SAME code path the command uses.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED BY THE SUITE, worth recording: the step-up ref parser first split on `rest.indexOf(":")`. An ISO instant carries two colons of its own, so every timestamp was truncated to its hour ("2026-08-10T23") and EVERY valid ref was refused — four tests went red with RECOVERY_COMPLETION_APPROVAL_INVALID on the positive path. The existing `approval.decide` handler is NOT routed through — TSDoc states why (it binds exactRevisionHash to a planning run's submissionHash).

PROJECT AND INCARNATION BINDING: both are length-framed components of the digest preimage, so an approval bound to another project's or another incarnation's evidence yields a different hash and is refused as a digest mismatch. TSDoc says explicitly that there is deliberately NO second comparison against caller-named refs — a check a caller could satisfy by restating its own request is not a binding.

WITNESS, built exactly as core's validRecovery demands and entirely server-derived: coverageProofHash = recoveryCoverageProofDigest over the record's configuredClasses + ordered proofs; inventoryReconciliationHash = the record's own recordDigest; recoveryDecisionRef = the verified approval's approvalRef; recoveryIncarnationRef = the record's anchored incarnationRef; truthClass = the literal "HUMAN_APPROVED" written in this module, never forwarded — and the payload has no key that could carry it anyway.

reduceProject then runs on the SERVER-read project state and its refusal code is surfaced verbatim at layer PROJECT_REDUCER. One store.commitExpectedVersionDecision writes the single ProjectRecovered event (eventId `recovery-complete:<commandId>:recovered`, store-wide unique) and the decision result together at targetAggregateId = projectId. A thrown DurableStoreError or a non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED disposition maps to RECOVERY_COMPLETION_STALE with the store code in upstream. Nothing is written on any refusal path: every gate returns a local refusal and the commit is constructed only after all of them pass.

REPLAY is answered at stage (B), BEFORE evidence — deliberately. A retry arrives after the project is already READY, so an evidence-first order would refuse an idempotent retry with EVIDENCE_MISMATCH instead of replaying it. The replay path re-reads the committed ProjectRecovered event and returns ITS witness rather than echoing the caller (the df29871b lesson), verifies the stored decision is this command's kind, aggregate and EFFECTS_COMMITTED, and refuses EVIDENCE_MISMATCH when the stored event binds a different reconciliation record.

DEFECT 1 — A STRAY NUL BYTE IN A PRODUCTION SOURCE, invisible to every gate. `grep` reported recovery-completion-digest.ts as a BINARY FILE; a byte count found exactly one 0x00 at offset 6261, line 144: `return value === null ? frame("\x00") : frame(\`s${value}\`)`. It is also self-contradictory: this module's own header forbids a NUL separator because the store's identifier validation rejects one. Replaced with `frame("n")`; null now frames as "n" and a present value as "s"+value, so the string "null" ("snull", 5 bytes) can never collide with absence ("n", 1 byte). Swept all 12 owned files: NUL count 0 everywhere.

LITERAL CLAUSE: "Hard dependencies: task-5606947a9d7d4f228dc63e6ce4dea69a, task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683, task-8a01c025b65246aca09e69d82e009587, and task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa must be DONE and consumed."

MEASURED — three of four are met, which is exactly why this one is easy to promote by mistake:
- task-5606947a (Cursor-bound complete backup generation) = DONE
- task-b6e3dd2a (Crash-safe two-slot recovery anchor installer) = DONE
- task-8a01c025 (Recovery-incarnation command authentication fence) = DONE
- task-cf7fb147 (Recovery inventory quarantine coordinator) = **BLOCKED** — NOT met

A 3-of-4 clause is still an unmet clause. task-cf7fb147 was independently re-audited today against the 17 tasks that closed on 2026-08-15 and came back genuinely gated, so this is not stale information.

NOTE THE SECOND HALF OF THE CLAUSE, which is stricter than a status check and is the part most likely to be skipped: the four dependencies must be "DONE **and consumed**". Consumed means a real production consumer edge exists, not merely that the producing task reached DONE. Under Clause 1, exporting symbols is not composition, and the runtime-loadability gate proves a package LOADS while nothing proves anything IMPORTS it. When task-cf7fb147 lands, verify each of the four by grep to a real production call site before planning — three DONE flags do not establish three consumer edges.

DO NOT RE-PROMOTE UNTIL task-cf7fb147 is DONE and all four dependencies are verified consumed on disk.

NOTE ON AUTHORITY: governor-74ff6cb3 drives board state and promoted this task; I hold an audit role and acted only because the human authorised it. If the promotion was deliberate, record that reasoning here before this moves again.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: BLOCKING on task-cf7fb147bd1c47698cbd65c9535370aa was measured, presented to the human, and explicitly OVERRULED: the direction was to take the full production path without blocking. That is workable because the capability this task actually consumes from the inventory area — a durable, digest-addressed RecoveryReconciliationRecord carrying truth, coverage proofs, item dispositions and quarantineRefs — is already shipped by the DONE inventory chain (task-00956ac3, task-091c93db, task-d7da9be4, task-47eecd22, task-f6cf8d16). What cf7fb147 still owes is the quarantine RESOLUTION path, and this task only ever REFUSES on unresolved quarantine, so it does not need one. Rejected: routing the recovery approval through the existing `approval.decide` handler — that handler binds exactRevisionHash to a planning run's submissionHash (planning-services.ts:163-161) and is the J1 plan journey, not a recovery approval. Rejected: changing `deriveRecoveryReconciliationTruth` so QUARANTINED yields UNKNOWN — that file is foreign-owned by the DONE task-f6cf8d16 and its output feeds the record digest, so editing it would alter a shipped durable surface; this service refuses quarantined items itself instead, which is exactly what DoD 3 asks for. Rejected: wiring `recovery.reconcile_external` (the writer command) in this task — it needs its own adapter module plus bridge, which would put the plan at 11-12 distinct files, and "enumerating external state" is this task's explicit NOT-in-scope. Landing the daemon-root export of the ledger here gives that future task a reachable surface instead of an island. Rejected: asserting embargo release through task-e33747f9's activation-embargo module — it is WORKING and unlanded; asserting the project state it reads is equivalent and uncoupled.

planningNotes.risks:
1. KNOWN OPEN GAP, recorded rather than hidden per the human's decision to proceed: no production command writes a RecoveryReconciliationRecord. The contract already reserves RECOVERY_RECONCILIATION_COMMAND_KIND = "recovery.reconcile_external" (recovery-inventory-contract.ts:28) and it has never been wired. This task's tests drive the real production writer `recordRecoveryReconciliation` directly — a shipped surface, not a mock — so DoD 6 holds, but until that command is wired the accept path is not reachable from HTTP ingress. The daemon-root export landed in step 7 is what makes wiring it a small follow-up. Flag this to the governor when handing off.
2. LIVE FILE COLLISION: task-e33747f9 is WORKING in apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry.ts and .test.ts right now, moving the closed ROWS table 20 -> 21. Step 8 must re-read both files from disk at that moment. Never restore an earlier snapshot over them; a foreign whole-tree commit that captures your bytes is a known hazard to disclose, not repair.
3. The quarantine gate is the DoD clause most likely to ship unenforced, because a COMPLETE record legitimately carries QUARANTINED items today. Drill B exists for exactly this. A no-op body has no operator to flip — if the drill stays green, make the body throw.
4. Refusal precedence is the whole point of task rail 4: where several layers can refuse, the test must pin WHICH answered first. A test asserting only `!ok` is one added layer away from vacuous.
5. Never let a caller supply truthClass, the accepted digest, the incarnation ref, or the witness hashes. Every one is server-derived; DoD 1 says the caller cannot supply the accepted digest as authority, and validRecovery pinning truthClass in core is a backstop, not the fence.
6. The digest preimage must be length-framed per component and use a separator that is a legal identifier character. A bare concatenation makes distinct tuples collide; a NUL separator is rejected downstream by the store's requireIdentifier while every local test stays green.
7. Windows/SQLite: open the store inside beforeEach or it, never a describe body — a held handle kills the vitest worker and afterAll rmSync then fails.
8. Shared worktree: a repo-wide red may be an untracked peer file that git diff and git log both hide. Attribute by merge-base-vs-HEAD failing-path delta intersected with owned paths before completing.
